title: Jamestown Holiday Guide
intro: Everything for the holidays on the island and just over the bridges, from Thanksgiving week through New Year’s Day: times, addresses, prices and what to expect.

sections.label: Saturday, Dec. 5: The Island's Big Holiday Day

items.where: Church at Four Corners (Central Baptist Church)
items.note: The church’s yearly fair at the Four Corners opens the day. In past years it has offered gift baskets, fresh evergreen wreaths, baked goods, a Re-gift Table and handmade gifts from more than a dozen Rhode Island crafters.
items.more: Last year’s lunch menu was soup, chili and hot dogs. The church calendar lists 9 to 2 this year; last year’s fair closed at 1, so come early for the wreaths.

items.t: Friends of the Library Winter Book Sale
items.note: The Friends of the library hold their seasonal book sale on Stroll day, a good stop for stocking-stuffer books.
The Chamber of Commerce’s Stroll fills the village with business open houses, holiday sales and treats, window displays, and craft fairs at local churches and schools.
items.more: Shops and fairs keep their own hours. Chamber: 401-423-3650.

items.note: A juried market of one-of-a-kind work by local artists and artisans: ceramics, jewelry, textiles, paintings, prints and more.
items.more: Bring a canned good or shelf-stable food for the Martin Luther King Jr. Community Center in Newport; bins are in the lobby. The building is wheelchair accessible.

items.note: The lighthouse museum and gift shop reopen for holiday shopping: lighthouse ornaments, mugs and books.
items.addr: Beavertail State Park, Beavertail Road, Jamestown
items.more: Also open Dec 6, 12 and 13. Museum phone: 401-423-3270.

items.t: Santa and Mrs. Claus Arrive by Boat
items.note: The Coastal Queen docks at East Ferry at 1 p.m. sharp. Santa and Mrs. Claus then ride a fire truck up to the Conanicut Gift Shop for visits and photos from 1 to 2 p.m.
items.addr: 1 East Ferry Wharf; photos at Conanicut Gift Shop, 20 Narragansett Ave.
items.more: Get to the wharf a little before 1 to see the boat come in.

items.t: Holiday Cruise with the Very Merry Dickens Carolers
items.note: Right after Santa docks, the Coastal Queen heads back out for a 75-minute cruise with the Dickens Carolers singing traditional carols. The center bar serves holiday drinks, beer, wine and soft drinks.
items.price: Newport sailings: $44 adults, $39 seniors and military, $34 children
items.more: Book with Coastal Queen Cruises: 401-423-9900.

items.note: The town tree lights up at East Ferry, with live music and Boy Scout Troop 1 luminaries along the seawall and Narragansett Avenue.
items.addr: East Ferry Wharf, Conanicus Ave., Jamestown
items.more: It is right on the water, so dress warmly.

items.note: A half-mile path of holiday lights around The Breakers grounds, with music, plus a look inside the decorated mansion on the same ticket.
items.more: Nights: Nov 21, 22, 27, 28, 29; Dec 3–6, 10–13, 18, 20–23, 26, 27. Timed entry at 4, 4:30, 5, 5:30 and 6; grounds close at 8. Tickets are for a set date and time and are not refundable.

items.t: Holidays at the Newport Mansions open
items.note: Three mansions dressed for Christmas, including the famous poinsettia tree at The Breakers. The Breakers and Marble House are open daily; Chateau-sur-Mer weekends only.
items.addr: The Breakers, 44 Ochre Point Ave.; Marble House, 596 Bellevue Ave.; Chateau-sur-Mer, 474 Bellevue Ave.
items.more: In past years the mansions closed on Thanksgiving and Christmas Day and at 2 p.m. on Christmas Eve.

items.note: Newport Contemporary Ballet’s Nutcracker moves through Rosecliff’s rooms, with the audience following the story; the second act is in the Grand Ballroom with reserved seats.
items.more: Opens Wednesday, Nov 25, at 5:30 p.m.; then matinee and evening shows Nov 27, 28, 29 and Dec 1–4. Ages 6 and up. Small audiences; it usually sells out.

items.t: A Rough Point Holiday: After Dark
items.note: Doris Duke’s oceanfront house, decorated for the season and open after dark.
Lit-up boats circle Newport Harbor the night after Thanksgiving, competing for best sailboat, powerboat and fishing boat.
items.more: Good viewing from Perrotti Park, Bowen’s Wharf and Bannister’s Wharf.

items.note: A tree lighting with Santa, photos, children’s crafts, letters to Santa and music.
items.more: Rain date Sunday, Nov 29.

items.note: The Goat Island lighthouse lights up for the season, with carolers, hot chocolate for the children and cider.

items.t: Candy Cane Express Cruise with Mrs. Claus
items.note: One-hour family sailings from Jamestown with Mrs. Claus aboard for the little ones.
items.more: Book with Coastal Queen Cruises: 401-423-9900.

items.note: A holiday brunch with Santa on Goat Island.

sections.label: On the Island: Concerts, Parties and Shopping

items.t: Holiday Arts Market Pre-Party and Early Shopping
items.note: First pick of the market the night before the Stroll.
More afternoons to shop the lighthouse gift shop, closed since fall.
items.more: Ask about the Beavertail charity license plate: $43.50 a set, $20 of it to the lighthouse.

items.t: A Contemporary Christmas: Jamestown Community Chorus
items.note: The island’s chorus, founded in 1949, sings a holiday program of mostly 21st-century music with a few folk tunes.
items.more: Chorus contact: 401-787-4487.

items.t: Narragansett Café Annual Christmas Party with The Renegades
items.note: The Ganny’s yearly Christmas party, with Amber Rose and The Renegades.

items.t: Christmas Eve at the Island Churches
items.note: St. Matthew’s Episcopal, Central Baptist and St. Mark Catholic all hold Christmas services; each posts its Christmas Eve and Christmas Day times in December.
items.addr: St. Matthew’s, 87 Narragansett Ave.; Central Baptist, 99 Narragansett Ave.; St. Mark, 60 Narragansett Ave.
items.more: We will add the times here as the churches post them.

items.note: A two-hour workshop with Petra Napolitano to sew your own stuffed ornaments.
items.more: Ages 13 and up; younger children with a parent. Registration required.

items.note: Make a fresh wreath with the Preservation Society’s greenhouse staff.
Drop in and paint a ceramic ornament to take home.
items.more: All ages; under 12 with a parent.

items.note: Learn a few side dishes for the holiday table.

items.t: Cookie Decorating and Spanish Fun with Solé
items.note: Kids practice beginner Spanish while decorating two cookies to take home.
items.more: Kindergarten through grade 4. Registration required.

sections.label: Over the Bridge in Newport and Middletown

items.t: On the Farce Day of Christmas
items.note: Ken Levine’s holiday comedy: a divorced daughter pays her ex to play husband at her parents’ house in Utah for Christmas.
items.more: Play and dinner packages available; check the Playhouse for times.

items.note: Newport’s month-long Christmas celebration, running every December since 1971, with events nearly every day.
items.more: It traditionally opens with the Washington Square tree lighting, a proclamation from the mayor and a Newport Artillery cannon salute.

items.t: Luminaria and Festival of Lights at Salve Regina
items.note: About 1,000 luminarias at Our Lady of Mercy Chapel and the 24th annual multi-faith Festival of Lights at Ochre Court, with music, dance and prayers.
Holiday shopping inside the historic Colony House.

The 56th annual lighting: Santa and live music from about 12:30, local musicians and choruses through the afternoon, and the tree lighting at 6 p.m. Santa and Mrs. Claus arrive by boat, weather permitting.
Beloved carols and contemporary choral works, presented by Newport Classical.
Handel’s Messiah in the Rosecliff ballroom, presented by Newport Classical.
Colonial-style decorations, live music, a traditional wassail bowl and a festive treat from the Colonial Dames.

items.t: Glen Manor House Christmas Open House
items.note: The manor opens to the public dressed in its holiday decorations.
A morning tour of how the mansions are decorated for the holidays.

items.t: The Irish Tenors: A Family Christmas
items.note: The Irish Tenors bring their family Christmas show to Washington Square.

items.t: Pictures with Santa and ‘A Visit from St. Nicholas’
items.note: Photos with Santa and readings of the classic poem.

items.t: Christmas Open House, Museum of Newport Irish History
items.note: The museum’s 10th annual open house, with eggnog and cookies.
An 11-piece chamber orchestra plays Bach, Vivaldi, the Nutcracker Suite and a Christmas sing-along.

items.t: Holiday Cruises with the Dickens Carolers from Newport
items.note: 75-minute caroling cruises on the Coastal Queen.
items.price: $44 adults; $39 seniors and military; $34 children and youth

items.note: About an hour on a decorated boat with Santa, hot chocolate and holiday music.
items.more: Sailings: Dec 14 at 2; Dec 19 at 11; Dec 20 at 11 and 1; Dec 21, 22 and 23 at 11. Book: 401-423-9900.

items.t: A Musical Retelling of ‘A Christmas Carol’ with Christine Baranski
items.note: One night only: the vocal ensemble Skylark sings the story, narrated by actress Christine Baranski.

items.t: A Christmas Carol at Trinity Rep
items.note: Trinity Rep’s 50th-anniversary production of Rhode Island’s best-known holiday play.
The Bristol mansion decorated room by room, with the evening Sparkle! light display on the grounds.
items.more: Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas.

items.t: ’Twas the Night Before… by Cirque du Soleil
items.note: Cirque du Soleil’s holiday family show: acrobatics, dance, characters and Christmas music.
items.more: Weekend shows at 1, 4 and 7:30 on Saturdays; PPAC has a family-ticket offer.

items.note: Thousands of white lights in the old village. Tree lighting at Updike Park opens it Thursday; Santa arrives by boat at the Town Dock on Brown Street Friday evening, and again Saturday and Sunday afternoons with carols and horse-drawn hayrides.
items.more: Elf Parade on Saturday; hot cocoa from the Boy Scouts; shops open until 9 p.m. Friday and Saturday.

items.note: The garden trails become a winter wonderland of decorated trees, with children’s activities, caroling, music, cocoa and handmade local gifts.
items.more: Last season it was open 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. on most Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays, and children’s tickets were $8. Check the garden for this year’s days.

items.note: Bristol lights its town tree at Hope and Court streets, with local school performers.
items.more: Rain date Dec 6.

items.t: Boston Pops Holiday Concert with Keith Lockhart
items.note: Keith Lockhart leads “Sleigh Ride,” seasonal arrangements, a sing-along and a visit from Santa.
Clara’s Christmas Eve story with Tchaikovsky’s score, Ballet RI dancers and local young performers.
items.more: Shows: Dec 17 and 18 at 7; Dec 19 and 20 at 1 and 6:30; Dec 23 at 6:30; Dec 26 at 1 and 6:30; Dec 27 at 1.

items.note: Hundreds of plungers run into the ocean at noon to raise money for A Wish Come True, which grants wishes to children with life-threatening illnesses.
items.more: Held every New Year’s Day; 2027 details are not posted yet. Parking is limited, so arrive early.
